title: The Covenant Beginning to Be Fulfilled
summary: The narrator teaches that when these sayings come to the Gentiles, the covenant concerning Israel’s restoration is beginning to be fulfilled, and the Lord’s words will all be fulfilled.

explicit_facts.text: The sayings will come to the Gentiles according to the Lord’s word.
The covenant concerning the restoration of the children of Israel to their lands of inheritance is beginning to be fulfilled when the sayings come forth.
The Lord’s words spoken by the holy prophets will all be fulfilled.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A written record may be shown to suggest the sayings coming forth.
unspecified_visual_details: The record’s physical appearance and the setting.

narration.text: when the Lord shall see fit

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The covenant’s fulfillment is described as beginning, not completed.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord, Israel’s restoration, or any historical prophet as visibly present; the verses do not describe their appearance or a present event.

title: The Lord Remembers His Covenant
summary: The narrator teaches that the Lord will remember his covenant with the house of Israel.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord will remember the covenant he made with his people of the house of Israel.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A written record may be shown as a visual aid for the narrator’s teaching.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting and any record’s appearance.

narration.text: the Lord will remember his covenant

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a teaching, not a narrated visible event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord or the house of Israel as visibly present.

title: Warning Against Spurning the Lord’s Doings
summary: The passage warns against spurning the Lord’s doings when these sayings come forth and pronounces woe on those who spurn his doings or deny Christ and his works.

explicit_facts.text: The warning says that when these sayings come forth, people need not spurn the Lord’s doings; it speaks of the sword of his justice overtaking those who spurn his doings.
Woe is pronounced on those who spurn the Lord’s doings and those who deny Christ and his works.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The warning can be presented as text without depicting a physical sword or punishment.
unspecified_visual_details: The identity and appearance of any speaker.

narration.text: the sword of his justice is in his right hand
Wo unto him that spurneth at the doings of the Lord; yea, wo unto him that shall deny the Christ and his works!

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The sword of justice appears in a warning, not in a narrated act of combat.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an attack, injury, or punishment as occurring.
Do not invent a visible appearance for the Lord or Christ.

title: Warning Against Denying Revelation
summary: The narrator warns against denying the Lord’s revelations and gifts, and against claiming for gain that Jesus Christ can work no miracle.

explicit_facts.text: Woe is pronounced upon those who deny the Lord’s revelations or say he no longer works by revelation, prophecy, gifts, tongues, healings, or the power of the Holy Ghost.
Woe is pronounced upon those who say for gain that no miracle can be wrought by Jesus Christ; the verse compares such a person to the son of perdition.

unspecified_visual_details: The setting and the identity of anyone addressed by the warning.

narration.text: the Lord no longer worketh by revelation
there can be no miracle wrought by Jesus Christ

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The listed revelations and gifts are part of a warning, not separate narrated miracle scenes.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a miracle, the son of perdition, or a person making these claims as a present event.

title: Do Not Mock the House of Israel
summary: The narrator teaches that people need not mock the Jews or any remnant of Israel, because the Lord remembers his covenant and will fulfill it; his judgment cannot be turned aside.

explicit_facts.text: People need not hiss at, spurn, or mock the Jews or any remnant of the house of Israel; the Lord remembers his covenant and will do as he swore.
People cannot turn the Lord’s right hand to the left to prevent his judgment and fulfillment of his covenant with the house of Israel.

unspecified_visual_details: The setting and any people being addressed.

narration.text: the Lord remembereth his covenant unto them

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The hand imagery is figurative teaching, not a visible act.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict mockery, judgment, or the fulfillment of the covenant as a present event.
